newsitem.title: USA: Oppenheimer raises Mexico to overweight from under.
newsitem.headline: Oppenheimer raises Mexico to overweight from under.

text.p: Oppenheimer & Co said on Friday it had raised its weighting on Mexico in its Latin American stocks portfolio to overweight from underweight and said Mexican stocks could rally 15-20 percent in the coming weeks.

Vinod Sehgal, Oppenheimer's director of research for Latin America, said the downside risk on Mexican stocks over the next few weeks was five percent, and short-term Mexican interest rates had a "decent chance" of declining to 25 percent from Thursday's high of 31 percent.
"We had been concerned earlier this (autumn) about the peso and about too much investor enthusiasm in the market," Sehgal said. "Our scenario has come true."
He said the Mexican stock market had corrected about 14 percent since its peak in August. He said 10 percent of that correction had taken place in October alone.
"From here we see the market having a 15 to 20 percent upside in the coming weeks," he said.
The catalysts for a rally will be a stable peso and lower short-term interest rates, he said.
"We expect the peso to stabilize at eight to a dollar. It appears that the central bank may have intervened to stabilize the peso, and we expect them to continue the course.
"We think that short-term interest rates have a decent chance of declining to 25 percent from 31 percent, which was the high yesterday," he said.
He said the potential downside for the Mexican stock market over the coming weeks was five percent.
